title: How to stop being a lazy slob (According to Reddit)
summary: NH walks through a Reddit post on training consistently without relying on just do it. Since beginners have weak willpower, they should get around it with four habit tactics: chaining, pre-commitment, removing barriers and small rewards. He then covers choosing a broad goal you love, avoiding deadlines, regular checkpoints and taking full responsibility, so you escape the loser's formula.
claims: Just do it is an empty truism with no method, and it frames training as a chore like doing dishes or taxes
For many serious lifters, lifting is the best part of the day and something to look forward to
Willpower is a skill built through repetition, not something you are born with; demanding willpower before someone has built it is circular

The loser's formula: jump in with no method, quit when it sucks, lose self-worth and become more likely to quit next time; the winner's formula is sticking with it, seeing results and gaining motivation
Sticking with one hobby for 10 years makes you better than 99% of people, even with no talent
Consistency beats both hard work and smart work; the guy who shows up every session wins, and every peak physique is built on it
Beginners need floaters, like learning to swim; get around weak willpower first, which will strengthen it over time
Most people avoid struggle, and their default answer to whether they want to train is no, so stop asking yourself the question and do not ask for your own consent
He knew an adult woman who skipped every other workday simply because she did not feel like going
Will is a finite reserve that grows with use; conserve it by building habits so you can draw on it when habits fail
Tactic 1, chaining: pair training with a habit you already have, e.g. lift before your 2 pm meal, so the habit chain is harder to break
Link training to positive habits like eating, a warm bath or a TV show; bad habits pair the same way, like cigarettes with coffee
Tactic 2, pre-commitment: keep an absolute schedule; he never skips training because it is on the schedule like work and lunch
Breaking promises to yourself feeds the loser's formula and wrecks your self-worth within a couple of weeks
Tactic 3, remove barriers: meal prep, follow any novice program (having structure matters more than which one at first) and plan location and transport ahead
Tactic 4, rewards: small, gym-related and immediate; he used to read one manga page during each rest period
Self-deprecation and negative reinforcement alone do not work long term; anger or rejection can get you started but is not sustainable
About 90% of people quit before the love of lifting kicks in
Novices going too hard is the top reason they crash and burn; his novice program is 3 days a week with easy rep ranges and no non-stop overload
Start with a broad goal like strength and size and specialise later; novice programs should not force a style on people
Choose a form of training you love; you cannot stick with something you hate
Do not set deadlines; finding what you love can take one to two years, and impossible goals breed despair (Kierkegaard's either Caesar or nothing)
Do not train only for the reward; sometimes you do everything right and nothing happens for a while
Use checkpoints to reassess; he trained for years thinking it was for size while actually training for strength and getting fatter
Every difficulty is your responsibility because only you can react to it; laziness is a developed trait, not your DNA, and you are not a loser, just someone who loses
A planned training session is halfway done, and an identified roadblock is halfway solved
